local.headline: Winter weather advisory runs to noon; Council delays MLGW rate votes
body: Action News 5 posted a winter weather advisory for portions of West Tennessee, East Arkansas and Southeast Missouri, in effect until noon Thursday. It calls for up to two inches of snow and warns that slick roads could affect the morning commute.

FOX13 Memphis reported that the Memphis City Council voted to put off action on MLGW's water and gas rate increase for two weeks. FOX13 also published a list of Thanksgiving week food giveaways around the Memphis area.

sources.title: Winter weather advisory for the Mid-South
Council delays MLGW water and gas rate vote

state.headline: Snow advisory for part of Middle Tennessee; flood grant deadline extended
body: WSMV posted a winter weather advisory for part of Middle Tennessee from 6 p.m. Thursday to noon Friday, with up to two inches of wet snow expected and slick roads possible for Friday morning travel.

The Chattanooga Times Free Press reported that Copperhill businesses hit by early November flooding now have until Dec. 11 to apply for an initial state recovery grant, according to state Rep. Dan Howell. Separately, Tennessee Lookout reported that a new federal scorecard shows the state trailing a national benchmark for having enough foster homes.

sources.title: Winter weather advisory for part of Middle Tennessee
More time for Copperhill flood recovery grants
Federal scorecard on Tennessee foster care

federal.headline: Administration proposes higher tariffs on China, EU and other partners
body: PBS NewsHour and CBS News reported that the Trump administration moved Wednesday to raise tariffs on major trading partners, including an added 20% on Chinese goods. PBS said the European Union, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan are among the others, and that the administration argues excess factory output abroad hurts American manufacturers.

PBS NewsHour also reported Commerce Department figures showing consumer prices in October up 3.8% from a year earlier, compared with 3.6% in September. In Iowa, ABC News and PBS NewsHour reported that officials saw encouraging early results, with no sign of spreading lead, after the Army detonated a stockpile of lead azide.

sources.title: Proposed tariff increases on trading partners
New tariffs planned for China, EU and others
Early lead readings after Iowa detonation

international.headline: Cairo highway fire after tanker crash kills at least 31
body: CBS News and the Associated Press reported that a fuel tanker crash sparked a large fire on a highway near Cairo, killing at least 31 people.

UN News reported that the U.N. aid chief, Tom Fletcher, arrived in Yemen on Wednesday and warned that fighting and supply route restrictions are keeping families from food and medicine. Separately, The Hill reported that an Iranian army spokesperson said, according to state media, that Iran is increasing surveillance and control over the Strait of Hormuz.

body: Markets were closed Thursday; these are Wednesday's closes from November 25. The S&P 500 fell 0.25%. The Dow rose 0.33%. The Nasdaq fell 0.62%.

The 10-year Treasury yield fell 6 basis points to 4.85%. Oil rose 0.75%. Gold rose 1.96%. The US Dollar Index rose 0.14%. A midday report from ABC News tied the choppy trading to a sell-off in some leading artificial intelligence companies.
